properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a Flood

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP, Texas
affecting Brewster County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village,
BBNP,  Texas...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP,
Texas.

* WHEN...From early this morning to mid morning.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, and no damage
is expected.  Preparations may be necessary to remove water pumps.
The park should be notified at this time if additional rises are
expected so they will have time to remove the pumps. At 13.0 feet,
the river reaches minor flood stage.  Water reaches the water pumps
maintained by the park service that are used to water the
campgrounds and to provide water to the employee living quarters.
It may be necessary for park personnel to remove the pumps. At 15.0
feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage.  Water pumps
submerge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 14.7 feet (4.5 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:30 PM CDT Tuesday was 14.7 feet (4.5 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 16.2 feet
(4.9 meters) early this morning. It will then fall below flood
stage later in the morning.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet (4.0 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.4
feet (5.0 meters) on 08/26/2016.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

tidal effects. River levels are forecast to gradually subside this
week but remain within Minor Flood stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.3 feet, Many docks become submerged along the river
and in canals in the Astor community. Water enters yards of
properties on Bartram Road, Holiday Circle and along Wild Hog Road
on the Lake County side. In Volusia County, water encroaches yards
of homes on the river side of Alice Drive. No wake zones are in
effect from near the South Moon Canal to approximately 800 feet
south of the Riverview lodge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EDT Tuesday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to very slowly subside from 2.6
feet tonight to 2.3 feet late this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.6
feet on 10/14/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 1100 AM EDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 29 at 5:53PM MST until September 30 at 5:45AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...
Apache County in northeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 545 AM MST /645 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks, normally dry washes and roadways is
imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 545 PM MST /645 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain.
Flooding is already occurring over area roadways in the warned
area, including the Navajo 71 roadway. In addition, the river
gage on the Little Colorado River at Holbrook is forecast to
exceed minor flood stage, which has impacted the railroad bridge
and caused overflow on the south bank of the river in the past.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Big Dam Wash, Polacca Wash, Beshbito Wash, Pueblo Colorado Wash,
Canyon Diablo Wash, Lithodendron Wash, Tees Toh Wash, Joseph City
Wash, Sabito Wash, Tanner Wash, Puerco River, Little Colorado
River, Steamboat Wash, Jeddito Wash, Tucker Flat Wash, Crazy
Creek, Coyote Wash, Bent Knee Wash, Cottonwood Wash, Diablo,
Canyon, Porter Tank Draw, Chevelon Canyon, Leroux Wash, Jacks
Canyon, Clear Creek, Oak Ridge Wash, Dead Wash and Bidahochi
Wash.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Winslow, Holbrook, Dilkon, Indian Wells, Tees Toh, Joseph City,
Sun Valley, Seba Dalkai, Manila, Hibbard, Greasewood Springs,
Clear Creek Reservoir, Bushman Acres, Cornfields, Klagetoh and
Wide Ruins.
- This includes the following highways...
Interstate 40 between mile markers 238 and 315. Business
Interstate 40 between mile markers 252 and 289. State Route 77
between mile markers 387 and 408. State Route 99 between mile
markers 31 and 71. State Route 87 between mile markers 326 and
385. Highway 191 between mile markers 376 and 397. Highway 180
between mile markers 308 and 309.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Homolovi State Park Campground, Hunt Park, McHood Park, Standin
on the Corner Park, Sacred Heart Park and Winslow City Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
